summary.title: Operations cheat sheet
summary.one_liner: A community-compiled PostgreSQL reference that explains the server's architecture, physical storage layout, processes, memory, WAL, transactions/MVCC, and connection troubleshooting, with links to further reading.
keywords: how does postgres process a query
takeaways: How a PostgreSQL cluster, databases, and tablespaces are organized, and what the data directory subfolders contain.
The roles of server processes (postmaster, backends, checkpointer, walwriter, autovacuum, walsender/walreceiver) and the shared vs. local memory areas.
How WAL, LSNs and MVCC (xmin/xmax) provide durability, crash recovery, and non-blocking reads.
A checklist for troubleshooting connection failures and configuring timeouts, keepalives, and connection limits.
summary.summary: This wiki page compiles community links and notes on PostgreSQL operations, organized as a reference rather than a step-by-step guide. It walks through client-server architecture, logical objects (cluster, databases, system catalogs, OIDs), and physical layout (data directory, relation forks, 8 KB pages and row format). It then covers server processes, memory areas, the read/write path, query processing stages, and connection troubleshooting and timeouts. The sections on WAL and transactions explain how WAL, XIDs and MVCC work. The page notes that it summarizes linked articles and that the originals should be read for detail.
